title: Precision pinboard and latency heatmap UX for model versioning
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a focused console UX that makes it fast and safe for engineers to: compare model versions, pin a version to a route, and publish/shadow performance profiles. The feature surface includes a ‘Precision Pinboard’ (compact chooser with key perf metrics) and a latency/throughput heatmap for quick visual comparison across versions and hardware targets.
background: Teams frequently run into two problems when promoting model versions: 1) they need a compact, low-noise UI to choose and lock a version for production routes without jumping across several pages; 2) performance profiles produced during onboarding are hard to relate to production traffic shape. Current console screens (version explorer, release gate) show lists and full perf dossiers but lack a lightweight chooser that surfaces unit economics and SLO risk side-by-side.
acceptance_criteria: Precision Pinboard is accessible from a route’s Version selector and loads within 200ms for 10 versions
Pinning flow: user can pin/unpin a version with one confirmation step; API call returns 200 and console shows pinned badge within 3s
Performance row: each version shows median latency (p50), p95, tokens/sec, and cost-per-1k-tokens based on stored profile
Latency heatmap: visual compares p50/p95 across versions and hardware flavors; users can toggle time window (last 24h/7d/30d)
Publish profile: users can publish a selected performance profile to the version (or keep as draft); publish action writes an audit log entry and surfaces a config diff
E2E validation: can perform a canary rollback via the pinboard when an alerted metric crosses configured threshold
Accessibility: keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels for all interactive elements
Unit tests for new UI components and integration tests for pin/unpin/publish actions exist in console repo
progress_updates: 2025-02-12 - Kickoff with PM, Design, and Runtime leads. Agreed scope: lightweight chooser + heatmap + publish flow (no rollout engine changes)
2025-02-18 - Design spike complete: low-fidelity pinboard + two heatmap variants (striped matrix vs. stacked bars). UX research scheduled with 6 backend engineers on 2025-02-25
2025-02-24 - Research notes: engineers prefer table-first view for quick scanning; visual heatmap useful for non-expert PMs. Decision to expose both compact table and expandable heatmap panel
2025-02-27 - Eng estimates: front-end 3 pts, backend API surface (audit + publish) 2 pts. Blocker: need minor extension to perf profile schema to include cost-per-thousand token metric
2025-03-01 - Design review: incorporate canary rollback CTA and audit toast. Design OK-ed pending microcopy tweaks. Engineering assigned to implement API endpoints for publish and pinning
engineering_notes: Backend: add POST /routes/{route_id}/pin with body {version_id, actor, reason} and record audit log; ensure idempotency
Backend: add POST /models/{model_id}/versions/{version_id}/profiles/{profile_id}/publish to atomically mark profile as published and update derived cost metric
API: new lightweight GET /routes/{route_id}/version-choices that returns precomputed perf summary for top N versions to keep payload small
Frontend: implement compact table with virtualized rows; heatmap panel should render with canvas for perf; metrics tooltips show raw sample counts
Trade-off considered: embedding full perf dossier increases load time; chosen approach fetches only summary and lazily loads full profile when user expands
decisions: Expose both a compact table and an expandable heatmap rather than replacing existing version explorer
Publishing a profile will not trigger rollout changes automatically; it only updates the published profile attached to a version
Pin action is separate from rollout traffic split: pinning sets sticky version for a route and is reversible via the pinboard rollback CTA
risks: Confusion between 'publish profile' and 'promote version' — mitigated via microcopy and confirmation dialog
Performance: heatmap rendering could be slow on very large version sets — limited to top 25 versions and virtualized canvas
Audit/Compliance: pinned changes must be recorded and surfaced in exportable audit logs
